turns.en: I think it's going to be transformational and I think this is an area that I'm surprised so few people have discussed about how AI is going to reinvent HR in the organizations.
turns.zh: 我觉得这会是变革性的，我很惊讶几乎没什么人讨论 AI 将如何重新发明组织里的人力资源（HR）。

turns.en: Because if you look at it the way it is today or for most organization is your manager gives you feedback every six months, tells you what you're doing well, what you're not doing well.
turns.zh: 因为如果你看今天的做法、大多数组织的做法，是你的经理每六个月给你一次反馈，告诉你哪里做得好、哪里做得不好。

turns.en: Generally, there's a lot of recency bias. So it's not really six months. It's like the last 30 days, what you did in the last 30 days, that's good or not.
turns.zh: 通常里面有大量近因偏差（recency bias），所以那不是六个月，而是最近 30 天你做了什么，好还是不好。

turns.en: Generally, it's not very actionable. It's like, you're doing this well, you're doing not, maybe you should do better. When does the type of feedback you would be giving an Olympic athlete?
turns.zh: 通常它并不太可执行，比如你这个做得好、那个做得不好，也许你应该做得更好。这种反馈你会给一个奥运运动员吗？

turns.en: That would be crazy. You would never be able to succeed. The Olympic athlete starts somebody that literally every day is coaching them and providing potential feedback.
turns.zh: 那会太疯狂了，你根本不可能成功。奥运运动员身边是一个每天都教练他们、给他们即时反馈的人。

turns.en: That is the opportunity that ultimately AI is going to create for every single person in an organization is you have Olympic athlete type of coaching.
turns.zh: 这正是 AI 最终会为组织里每一个人创造的机会：你得到奥运选手级的教练。

turns.en: And so what we're building a new bank in our HR operational system is literally every day, depending on where you are, if you're an engineer or a designer or a product manager, daily you should be able to get feedback from the AI, your AI co-pilot, if you're coding, is reviewing your pull requests and is telling you not only how you're using these tools, but how could you use them better?
turns.zh: 所以我们在 Nubank 的 HR 运营系统里做的事情，是字面意义上每天、根据你的岗位——工程师、设计师还是产品经理——你都应该能从 AI 得到反馈。你的 AI 副驾，如果你在写代码，它在 review 你的 pull request，不仅告诉你你怎么在用这些工具，还告诉你怎么更好地用它们。

turns.en: And it's very actionable and it's very specific to what you're doing. If you're a designer, is giving you feedback around how you're doing your job and how better you could do in your job.
turns.zh: 它非常可执行，而且非常针对你正在做的事。如果你是设计师，它会就你怎么做你的工作、怎样做得更好给出反馈。

turns.en: If you're a manager, managers right now have very little information, especially if you're managing a lot of people, that's the other thing about this large span of controls, there is this sense that you have to be having one-on-ones with every single person in your week.
turns.zh: 如果你是管理者，管理者现在掌握的信息非常少，尤其当你管很多人的时候——这也是大管理幅度带来的另一件事。人们总觉得要每周和团队里每个人做一次一对一。

turns.en: Those one-on-ones tends to be very low information density type of interchange. A manager that has access to all this information, this instrumentation is now seeing real time how every person in the team is actually doing and is allowing them to improve what they're doing.
turns.zh: 那些一对一往往是信息密度很低的交流。一个能接触到所有这些信息的、被仪表化（instrumented）的管理者，现在能实时看到团队里每个人实际上做得如何，并且能帮他们改进正在做的事。

turns.en: How do you stay up to speed on AI capabilities? Like, who are the people you rely on? What are the things you like to read? I feel like you need to time box it every day.
turns.zh: 你怎么跟上 AI 能力的步伐？你依赖哪些人？你喜欢读什么？我觉得你得每天给自己划出一个时间段。

turns.en: I can get one hour to read the updates or something. It's like a sports center for business. How do you do it? I'll spend a lot of time on X.
turns.zh: 哪怕只是一小时来读那些更新之类的。它就像商业界的体坛快讯（SportsCenter）。你怎么做？——我会花很多时间在 X 上。

turns.en: I think that's where you're seeing a lot of the development also. I have an agent that collates and summarizes a lot of the developments of what's going on on details.
turns.zh: 我觉得那里也是你看到大量进展发生的地方。我有一个智能体，把 X 上的大量动态汇总、摘要给我。

turns.en: I block specific time in my agenda to use these tools and to build products. This is something that I hadn't done for a very long time. I coded a non-custodial crypto app, for example.
turns.zh: 我在日程里专门留出时间去使用这些工具、去构建产品。这是我很久没做的事了。比如我写了一个非托管（non-custodial）的加密应用，

turns.en: That's something that we've discussed at Nubank for a very long time to do. I just went in and did a project. We asked all of our senior managers to build products every quarter on actual software and products so that we are integrated and very aware of what's going on.
turns.zh: 这是我们在 Nubank 讨论了很久要做的事，我就是直接动手做了一个项目。我们要求所有高级经理每个季度都用真正的软件和产品做出东西，这样我们才身处其中、清楚地知道正在发生什么。

turns.en: I don't think necessarily the answer is that I should be spending 70% coding. There are better people that will be much more productive coding than I am, but I think it's important for everybody in the organization to be actually not only reading, but actually using the tools actively to understand how fast the technology is going.
turns.zh: 我不觉得答案一定是我该把 70% 的时间花在写代码上——有比我更能干、写代码效率更高得多的人。但我认为对组织里每个人重要的是，不只是阅读，而是真正主动使用这些工具，去理解技术走得有多快。

turns.en: If you think back to the start, you and actually last time talked about this, what the original motivations were, and I mean not just the business opportunity, but the personal sources of drive, how has that evolved and what's it like today?
turns.zh: 回想开始的时候，你上次其实也聊过这个——最初的动机是什么，我说的不只是商业机会，而是个人层面的驱动力来源。它如何演化，今天是什么样子？

turns.en: I'm motivated by impact, by making it count, by doing something, we're investing time and energy in something that has a meaning and that has some kind of impact.
turns.zh: 我的动力来自影响、来自让这件事有意义、来自把时间和能量投入某件有含义、有某种影响的事。

turns.en: I went through a phase, even with new bank, where I started thinking, is there more stuff that I should be doing beyond new bank? I think all founders get starting on the company.
turns.zh: 我经历过一个阶段，即使在 Nubank 里面，我开始想：除了 Nubank，我是不是该做更多别的事情？我想所有创始人都会有——

turns.en: The company then has a significant growth and then you start asking your questions, what else could I be doing? Ultimately, I went through the other side of that analysis for about a year or two years, realizing that there's nothing else that I can imagine myself doing that could have more impact than taking new bank from where it is today to making it the next larger and going from three countries to a hundred countries or from a hundred million customers to a billion
turns.zh: 公司创立，然后有显著的增长，然后你开始问自己：我还能做什么？最终，我花了大概一到两年从另一个方向走完这个分析，意识到我想象不出还有别的什么事，能比把 Nubank 从今天的位子带到下一个更大的规模、从三个国家到一百个国家、从一亿客户到十亿客户——

turns.en: customers. What this means in terms of impacting financial services, impact for people around the world, for billions of people, access to financial services, and with that impact out there, it's impacting internally too.
turns.zh: 更有影响力。这对金融服务意味着什么，对全世界数十亿人获得金融服务意味着什么；而这种影响也向内部传导。

turns.en: It's like how I can also understand myself through bigger and newer challenges and how I can develop better as a leader to motivate an organization that has big ambitions and with big technology shifts, like AI can either decide to stay behind or stay in front.
turns.zh: 就像我如何也能通过更大、更新颖的挑战来理解自己，如何能成为一个更好的领导者，去激励一个有宏大野心、面对巨大技术变革的组织：AI 你可以选择落在后面，也可以站在前面。

turns.en: I think this technology shift forces every organization to think, in which side of this disruption do I want to be? I find that I'm more of a wartime general than a peace time general, and so when a disruption, a change in the world happens, it suddenly is a source of motivation.
turns.zh: 我想这次技术变革会迫使每一个组织思考：我想站在这场颠覆的哪一边？我发现自己更像战时将军而不是和平时期将军，所以当一场颠覆、一次世界的变化发生时，它突然就成了动力的来源。

turns.en: I get more energized to actually continue to execute that mission. What's an example of understanding yourself better because of growth? In what ways has that happened?
turns.zh: 我会更有能量去继续执行那个使命。有什么例子是你因为成长而更了解自己的？在哪些方面发生了？

turns.en: One of the questions that I personally had as I scaled the business is, will we need to bring much more professional managers at some point?
turns.zh: 我在扩张业务时个人遇到的一个问题就是：我们是否需要到某个时刻引入更多职业经理人？

turns.en: Because I didn't manage anybody before starting new bank, and then suddenly I found myself being the CEO of one of the largest banks in Latin America and asking myself, well, what does the organization need right now?
turns.zh: 因为创办 Nubank 之前我没管过任何人，然后突然之间我成了拉美最大银行之一的 CEO，然后问自己：组织现在需要什么？

turns.en: Do we need to go and hire a much more experienced manager? We did. We hired a lot of external talent because I concluded or thought that I was going to need that, but also then quickly realized that actually that's not what the organization needed.
turns.zh: 我们是不是要去请一位更有经验的管理者？我们做了。我们招了很多外部人才，因为我得出结论、或者说我以为我需要那样；但很快我也意识到，那其实不是组织需要的。

turns.en: What the organization needed was more of what I had already brought into the organization, which was this clear leadership, the motivation, the willingness to think really big and to dream very big and get people excited about doing something that feels impossible at the beginning.
turns.zh: 组织需要的是我本来已经带进组织的那些东西：清晰的领导力、动力、愿意想得非常大、梦得非常大，让别人为一件开始看起来不可能的事兴奋起来。

turns.en: Once something clicks and says, no, this is the right answer for me and for the organization, I can continue doing what I'm doing with much more confidence, especially when there's changes and shifts.
turns.zh: 一旦某件事咔哒一声通了，你说：不，这对我和对组织都是正确答案，我可以带着更多的自信继续做我在做的事，尤其是在有变化和转折的时候。

turns.en: There was always a little bit of a Latin question, am I pushing too hard? Am I asking too much from the team? Is this the right pace? The answer after 13 years of doing this and being a little bit more confident is, yes, I'm pushing enough.
turns.zh: 一直有个有点拉丁式的疑问：我是不是推得太狠了？我向团队要得太多了吗？这是对的节奏吗？做了 13 年、自信一点之后的答案是：是的，我推得够狠。

turns.en: It's my job to push very hard and to dream very big and to shoot very high, and then the organization will react and will push back if needed, but it's helpful to have somebody that is actively pushing the boundaries of what perhaps the company is ready to do.
turns.zh: 我的工作就是非常用力地推、梦想得非常大、瞄准得非常高，然后组织会反应、会在需要时反推回来。但有一个人主动去推动公司也许尚未准备好的边界，是有帮助的。

turns.en: What is the hardest part of doing that for a long period of time? The imposter syndrome. It's fine to be a founder at the beginning, but then suddenly when you see yourself running a very large organization, it's like, am I the right person relating this organization?
turns.zh: 长时间做这件事，最难的部分是什么？冒名顶替综合征（imposter syndrome）。

turns.en: You have to, through some thinking and through some experiences and through some feedback, answer that question for you at some point and answer it definitively on maybe for some reason you're not, but probably you are.
turns.zh: 你必须通过一些思考、一些经历、一些反馈，在某个时点为自己回答那个问题，并且给出确定的答案——也许出于某种原因你不是，但很可能你就是。

turns.en: That doesn't mean that necessarily at the founder will have all the answers and will have all the skills. You will need to continue bringing people that add a lot of complementary skills to you, but I think at least for me was surpassing that phase of having a voice in the head thinking, are you the right CEO for the business?
turns.zh: 那并不意味着创始人一定拥有所有答案、拥有所有技能。你需要继续引入能为你补充大量互补技能的人。但至少对我来说，是跨过那个阶段——脑子里有个声音在问：你是这家公司合适的 CEO 吗？

turns.en: And in making the shape between founder and CEO, because generally you will see founders having both titles, but they're very different functions.
turns.zh: 以及把创始人和 CEO 这两个角色分开，因为你通常会看到创始人同时拥有两个头衔，但它们是非常不同的职能。

turns.en: The founder and the CEO are very different functions that don't necessarily fit with each other. What's the key energy of each? The founder, it's impatient, huge amount of sense of urgency.
turns.zh: 创始人和 CEO 是非常不同的职能，未必彼此契合。各自的关键能量是什么？创始人不耐烦，有极强的紧迫感。

turns.en: The founder will want to go run very, very fast, will move fast, extremely fast. The CEO will need to be more patient. The CEO will need to be more systematic in how it makes decisions.
turns.zh: 创始人想跑得非常非常快，动作极快。CEO 则需要更有耐心，需要在做决策时更成体系。

turns.en: I will have to bring generally much more systems thinking into scaling the organization. And sometimes those things collude. If you have to be impatient on one end, you have to be patient on the other end, there might be conflicts in that nature.
turns.zh: 我在给组织规模化时，通常需要带入更多系统思维。有时候这两者会冲突：如果一边要你不耐烦、另一边要你耐心，那类矛盾就会出现。

turns.en: Generally you would think that CEOs are better managers. Founders don't tend to be good managers. Founders don't have a lot of patience or willingness to do one-on-ones and sit down and provide coaching to a team.
turns.zh: 通常会认为 CEO 是更好的管理者，创始人往往不是好管理者。创始人没什么耐心或意愿去做一对一、坐下来给团队做辅导。

turns.en: They just want to run. A lot of the time they tend to be much more ICs, individual contributors and managers. CEOs tend to be better managers because you have to build systems.
turns.zh: 他们只想跑。很多时候他们更像是独立贡献者（individual contributor）而不是管理者。CEO 往往是更好的管理者，因为你必须建立系统。

turns.en: You have to be thinking more from a system perspective. I think the key though for me has been to realize that the CEO title itself and the founder title, you can redesign in different ways too.
turns.zh: 你必须更多从系统的角度思考。不过对我来说关键的一点是意识到，CEO 这个头衔和创始人这个头衔本身也可以被重新设计。

turns.en: And it's being able to do both. It's being able to have a little bit more patience when you need a bit more patience. But generally you want to maintain more of the founder than the CEO.
turns.zh: 而关键在于两者都能做。在需要更多耐心的时候多一点耐心。但总体上，你想保留更多创始人的一面，而不是 CEO 的一面。

turns.en: And I think that's why founder-led companies continue to outperform for decades because if you have to choose, you choose more the founder than the CEO mode, especially in environments where there are big technology shifts, where a lot of the advantages, the assets of the founder come to bear and are more obvious than necessarily the advantages of the CEO.
turns.zh: 我想这就是创始人领导的公司能持续几十年跑赢的原因：如果必须选择，你会选择更偏创始人而不是 CEO 的状态，尤其是在有巨大技术变革的环境里——那里创始人的资产和优势更能发挥作用、更加明显，胜过 CEO 的优势。

turns.en: What was your lowest confidence moment personally in the entire history of the business? How'd you get through it? I think you go through a lot of different phases.
turns.zh: 在整个公司发展史上，你个人信心最低的时刻是什么？你怎么走过来的？我想你会经历很多不同的阶段。

turns.en: And I think scaling a business is hard, especially because you're consistently making decisions about situations that you don't really know.
turns.zh: 而且我觉得规模化业务很难，尤其是因为你一直在对其实并不了解的情况做决策。

turns.en: For example, I wanted to build a technology company, but I was not an engineer myself. So I needed to go and hire great CTOs and build a great technology organization.
turns.zh: 比如我想建一家科技公司，但我自己不是工程师。所以我得去招很棒的 CTO、建一个很强的技术组织。

turns.en: How did I know how to pick a great CTO at that point if I didn't have the experience or credit, whether it's a lot of specific to financial services and credit expertise?
turns.zh: 那时候我怎么知道怎么选一个优秀的 CTO？我并没有相关经验。信贷呢？那是大量特定于金融服务和信贷的专业能力。

turns.en: So there was a lot of questioning inside internally, a lot of the decisions that he made about building the team that made me ask myself the question, do we need to bring somebody with my experience from a big bank or from a big organization to run the organization?
turns.zh: 所以内部有很多自我质疑。在组建团队这件事上做的很多决定，都让我问自己：我们是不是需要从一家大银行、一个大组织请来一个经验比我丰富的人来经营组织？

turns.en: For a period of time, is this imposter syndrome that is asking you make question, is like, are you the right driver of the car as the car becomes more complex and goes faster and faster and faster and faster?
turns.zh: 有一段时间，那种冒名顶替综合征在问你、让你质疑：当这辆车越来越复杂、越来越快，你是不是那个合适的司机？

turns.en: What was the most emotional moment in the history of the business for you? Passing a number of different incumbent banks in Brazil was very emotional because for ten years all we heard again and again and again, especially from the local experts, was that it was impossible to compete with any bank, that we were going to get crushed, that we were going to die, that these were the most trusted brands in the ecosystem and that we
turns.zh: 在公司历史上对你来说最动情的时刻是什么？超越若干家在位银行非常让人动情，因为十年里我们反复听到的——尤其是那些本地专家说的——是：跟银行竞争是不可能的，我们会被碾碎，我们会死掉，它们是生态里最受信任的品牌，我们

turns.en: had no shot at being successful. Becoming the largest private bank in the entire country was something incredible. So it was emotional in terms of what we were able to achieve from a point of scale.
turns.zh: 毫无成功的机会。成为全国最大的私营银行是一件了不起的事。所以从规模成就的角度，它让人动情。

turns.en: Personally, I was born in Colombia and I had to live Colombia when I was eight because of all the security situation in Colombia as we grew up and I had to move to Costa Rica and Colombia was then our country number three.
turns.zh: 就我个人而言，我出生在哥伦比亚，八岁那年因为哥伦比亚的安全局势不得不离开，我们在哥斯达黎加长大，然后哥伦比亚成为我们开展业务的第三个国家。

turns.en: The moment that I was able to launch New Bank in Colombia, which we did in a big event with the president of the country at the same time, was very emotional as well because there was a bit of coming back home and delivering a product and a service that I thought was going to be very great for the country in an environment where I was being receptive by my people.
turns.zh: 当我能在哥伦比亚推出 Nubank 的那一刻——我们办了一场大活动，这个国家的总统同时出席——也非常动情，因为那有点像是回家，交付了一件我认为对这个国家非常好的产品和服务，而那里是我的人民接纳了我的地方。

turns.en: And it was video-casted and there were 100,000 people connected to the launch of New Bank in Colombia. It was very emotional too. It was very exciting.
turns.zh: 那次还做了直播，有 10 万人在线连接看 Nubank 在哥伦比亚的发布。那也很让人动情，非常让人兴奋。

turns.en: With all this experience now running the business, how would you define great leadership? And I'm especially interested in the subtle points of what defines in your opinion a great leader.
turns.zh: 有了现在经营这家公司的全部经验，你会如何定义卓越的领导力？我特别感兴趣的是那些微妙的点——在你看来是什么界定了一位伟大的领导者。

turns.en: With vision, you have to be able to see something that few people see, a world that is not as obvious right now. And I think with the massive information overload that we all live in, it's increasingly harder to have a differentiated point of view about something, about your industry, about your company, about how things are going to move.
turns.zh: 第一是愿景（vision）：你必须能看到少数人看到的东西，看到一个眼下并不显然的世界。我觉得在我们所有人都处在巨大信息过载的当下，要形成对某件事——你的行业、你的公司、事情将如何演变——的差异化观点，越来越难。

turns.en: So you have to have some kind of vision about the future that is differentiated. But then you have to be able to sell that vision. And selling is about inspiring people.
turns.zh: 所以你必须有某种差异化的未来愿景。然后你必须能把那个愿景卖出去。而卖，是关于激励人。

turns.en: And a lot of the time that vision will be very hard or almost feel impossible. And the natural reaction of most people when they are presented with an impossible vision is to push back and to declare it non-realistic, this phrase, it's not realistic that this is going to happen.
turns.zh: 很多时候那个愿景会非常难、几乎看起来不可能。大多数人在面对一个不可能的愿景时，本能反应是反驳、宣布它不现实——这句话，这不现实、这不会发生。

turns.en: What is not realistic? I mean, look at every single meaningful development in the history of the world. At some point, it was defined by somebody to be non-realistic, the amount of confidence that a lot of the experts or people use when they say it's not realistic.
turns.zh: 什么是不现实？看看世界历史上每一个有意义的发展，它在某个时点都被某个人判定为不现实。那么多专家或者普通人说这不现实时所用的那种自信。

turns.en: You have to be able to sell that vision in a way that a lot of people get motivated by that, that drives following and motivation. But then you have to be able to be a good listener and understand that sometimes you're actually going to be wrong.
turns.zh: 你必须能把那个愿景卖出去，让很多人被它激励，从而带来追随和动力。然后你还必须是一个好的倾听者，理解有时候你其实是错的。

turns.en: That vision that you have might not be fully complete. There is a mode in which you go against the consensus and you completely declare consensus as wrong and you are the complete revolutionary.
turns.zh: 你的那个愿景也许并不完整。有一种模式是你逆流共识，把共识彻底判定为错误，你做一个彻底的革命者。

turns.en: Nothing about the consensus makes any sense and you will reinvent absolutely everything. That is one mode. The other mode is you're consumed by consensus.
turns.zh: 共识里的一切都没有意义，你要重新发明所有东西。那是一种模式。另一种模式是你被共识吞没。

turns.en: You think about progress as being non-realistic and things will be the way they are today. What's hard I think about a great leader is you're navigating the middle.
turns.zh: 你觉得进步是不现实的，事情会永远像今天这样。我觉得伟大领导者的难处在于，你要走在中间。

turns.en: Consensus exists or status quo exists because you think about it from an evolutionary perspective. The vision of the world competed with all our visions of the world and it won.
turns.zh: 共识之所以存在、现状之所以存在，你从演化的角度想想：关于世界的这个观点在和所有其他观点的竞争中胜出并存活下来了。

turns.en: The world we see today was superior to our possible world that happened. There are elements of that status quo that exist because of a reason.
turns.zh: 我们今天看到的世界，优于当时可能发生的其他世界。现状里的某些元素之所以存在，是有原因的。

turns.en: You have to be able to understand what are those elements and they will continue to be here. But also, you have to be able to fight that conventional wisdom to see what are the elements will need to be changed.
turns.zh: 你必须能理解哪些元素是有原因、还会继续存在的；但同时你也必须能挑战那种传统智慧，看清哪些元素是需要被改变的。

turns.en: I think leadership is about knowing what doesn't have to change and pushing to change the things that have to change. That's a combination of conviction but also active listening and humility to know that you might not have all the answers and that you're going to need to change your mind actively when you do that.
turns.zh: 我想领导力在于知道什么不需要改变，同时拼命推动那些必须改变的东西。那是信念、主动倾听和谦逊的结合——知道自己也许没有全部答案，需要在该改主意的时候主动改主意。

turns.en: So, combining all those different factors I think is pretty critical for good leadership. If we think over the next five years for New Bank specifically, I'd love you to paint what you think is the bear case for the business and the case you worry about and are actively making sure it doesn't happen.
turns.zh: 所以把这些不同的因素结合起来，我认为是卓越领导力的关键。如果我们看 Nubank 未来五年，我希望你描述一下你认为的熊市案例（bear case）——那个你担心、并且正在主动避免发生的版本。

turns.en: Then, if I think about my rose-colored glasses on, the best possible story for New Bank over the next five years, I'd love to hear the two ends of the spectrum from your perspective.
turns.zh: 然后，如果我戴上玫瑰色眼镜（rose-colored glasses），Nubank 未来五年最好的故事会是什么——我很想听听你眼中的两个极端。

turns.en: The bear case is we are in these two countries in Latin America. We've saturated them completely, growth declines. We haven't really been able to find any other growth alternatives from a customer perspective.
turns.zh: 熊市案例是：我们在拉美这两个国家已经把它们彻底做饱和了，增长下滑；从客户角度我们没能找到任何其他增长替代。

turns.en: We have 65% of Brazil, very soon we're going to run out of Brazilians. Ideally, we would see the natality rate in Brazil in current people having more children but that's not happening.
turns.zh: 我们拿了巴西的 65%，很快我们就没有巴西人可以拿了。理想情况下，我们会看到巴西的出生率、现在的人多生孩子，但那没有在发生。

turns.en: So, we're going to run out of Brazilians. We did not succeed in internationalizing. We ended up being restricted to these three countries and growth saturated.
turns.zh: 所以我们会把巴西人用完。我们国际化没成功，最终被限制在这三个国家里，增长饱和。

turns.en: That's the bear case. Partly of that would also mean that we could not take advantage of a lot of the AI opportunities that enables also and so that's one reason why we're not able to internationalize.
turns.zh: 那就是熊市案例。其中一部分也意味着我们没能利用 AI 带来的很多机会；这也是我们无法国际化的一个原因。

turns.en: The bear case is the opposite of that is we truly took advantage of these thesis that we have around how much market share is going to be transferred from incumbent banks to digital and native companies over the next two to three decades and how that is going to be accelerated by technology shifts like real-time payment systems, open finance and AI.
turns.zh: 熊市案例的反面是：我们真正兑现了自己那个论断——未来二三十年里，市场份额会从在位银行向数字原生公司大规模转移，而且这个转移会被实时支付系统、开放金融和 AI 这些技术变革加速。

turns.en: We were able to ride those tailwinds from technology shifts and we were able to execute through a multi-country platform a global vision of new bank taking us to 100 plus countries over the next few decades and we were able to solve a lot of these big problems that we think that will be solved.
turns.zh: 我们搭上了这些技术变革的顺风，通过多国平台执行了 Nubank 的全球愿景，在未来几十年走到 100 多个国家，并且解决了我们认为是必然会被解决的那些大问题。

turns.en: 3 billion people don't have access to credit, cash is becoming digital, more people need access to banking. If we have these cost structure advantage versus our competitors versus the industry players that's still on 90% of the 10 trillion dollar profit pool, if we have a cost structure that is 50x theirs and this is pre-AI, then that meant we were able to pass a lot of the efficiency back to the customer via higher yields, lower fees, better experience, fully
turns.zh: 30 亿人拿不到信贷，现金正在数字化，更多人需要银行服务。如果相对竞争对手、相对仍占据 10 万亿美元利润池 90% 的那些行业玩家，我们有成本结构优势；如果我们的成本结构只有他们的五十分之一，而这还是 AI 之前的水平——

turns.en: digitalized, integrating advice in our products and truly taking advantage of these internationalization opportunities. So that is the bull case.
turns.zh: 那就意味着我们能把很多效率让渡给客户：更高的收益率、更低的费用、更好的体验、彻底数字化、把建议嵌入产品，并真正抓住这些国际化的机会。那就是牛市案例（bull case）。

turns.en: When I had you last time five years ago, I already asked you my traditional closing question so I have a different one for you today. Again, across New Bank and the incredible experience that you've had building it so far, what is the most interesting lesson that you've learned about entrepreneurship?
turns.zh: 五年前请你来那次，我已经问过我一贯的收尾问题，所以今天换一个。同样是在 Nubank 和你迄今建设它的这段非凡经历里，关于创业你学到的最有意思的一课是什么？

turns.en: How to quickly ignore the imposter syndrome and how the fact that you are the person that had the vision and the energy to build something out of nothing, to give birth, that already is giving you a level of care for that company so high that it will make you become the right leader for a very long time.
turns.zh: 如何快速无视冒名顶替综合征；以及这样一个事实——你是那个有愿景、有能量从无到有把东西建起来、给它生命的人，这本身已经给了你对这家公司极高的在意程度，它会让你在很多年里都成为正确的领导者。

turns.en: I don't think anybody in the world cares as much for this company as I do, right? To a level that is almost miserable. You're a father, right?
turns.zh: 我不觉得世界上有任何人像我这样在乎这家公司，在乎到近乎痛苦的程度。你是父亲，

turns.en: You have children. Nobody will ever care so much about this company, about this company being successful. Then I will and that will make you put so much energy and focus to make it successful to the point that ultimately is what is going to make you be the right leader for the organization for a very long time independently of your expertise or your knowledge or whether you have the right experience.
turns.zh: 你有孩子。没有人会比我更在乎这家公司、更在乎它成功。这会让你投入巨大的能量和专注去让它成功，最终正是这一点，会让你在很长时间里都是这个组织合适的领导者，不论你的专业能力、你的知识、你有没有合适的经验。

turns.en: Just that insight, just that energy will make you the right person. It seems like you could decompose that into have more faith in yourself and be really persnickety about the vision that you want to go work on because if it's not something that's coming deep from your heart, from your gut, you won't get the benefit of this thing you just laid out.
turns.zh: 就是这个洞见，就是这股能量会让你成为对的人。我觉得这可以拆成两部分：对自己有更多信念，同时对你要去做的那个愿景极度挑剔——如果它不是从你心底、从你的直觉里涌出来的，你就得不到你刚才说的这个好处。

turns.en: Do you think those are the right two parts of that really interesting insight? Yeah, especially the second part you mentioned around the mission.
turns.zh: 你觉得那是那个有意思洞见里正确的两部分吗？是的，特别是你提到的第二部分——使命。

turns.en: That's a luxury and a blessing to find a mission that you truly are excited about because then that will really make you go the long way. Scaling a company won't be easy.
turns.zh: 找到一个你真正为之兴奋的使命是一种奢侈和幸运，因为那才是真正让你走完全程的东西。规模化一家公司不容易。

turns.en: It will be much more painful than anybody anticipates and if you don't have the level of conviction for the mission, it will be just harder to go.
turns.zh: 它会比任何人预想的都痛苦；如果你对使命没有那种程度的信念，你就更难走下去。

turns.en: How would you encourage other people to do a good job on that search? Like if someone's searching for a mission that's perfect for them, any advice that you would give them or any sign that they've got the right one?
turns.zh: 你会怎么鼓励别人把这场寻找做好？如果有人正在寻找最适合他们的使命，你会给他们什么建议，或者有什么迹象说明他们找到了对的那个？

turns.en: There is a level of certainty there in luck. There is a level of search, of listening carefully, of feeling that this is a project, this is a problem that you truly care about.
turns.zh: 这里面有一定程度的确定性，也有运气。有某种程度的寻找、认真的倾听，去感觉到这个项目、这个问题是你真正在乎的。

turns.en: This is something that if you really care about, you are not sleeping because you're thinking about it. You cannot imagine your life continuing if you do not decide to tackle it.
turns.zh: 它是那种你真的在乎到睡不着觉、一直在想的事。如果你不去解决它，你无法想象自己的生活继续下去。

turns.en: I think AI makes it harder, not easier just because the bar to start a company is now so much easier. You were probably just going to go and pursue problems that are easier to solve ultimately.
turns.zh: 我觉得 AI 让这件事更难而不是更容易，只是因为创办公司的门槛现在低太多了，你最终很可能只是去追那些更容易解决的问题。

turns.en: I think that's why some of the best founders that we're seeing right now are going for the impossible truly. There is this shift now into hardware and space and things that seem completely impossible because you're looking actively for those opportunities that will be harder and unique to you that you're going to get to believe that only you can really solve.
turns.zh: 我想这就是为什么我们现在看到的一些最好的创始人真的在追不可能。现在有一波转向硬件、太空和那些看似完全不可能的事情，因为你主动去找那些更难的、对你独特的、你会相信只有你能解决的机会。
